name: Adobo
blurb: Meat, usually chicken or pork, braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, peppercorns and bay leaf until the sauce turns dark and glossy. Nearly every household has its own version.
visual: dark brown pieces of braised meat in a glossy soy and vinegar sauce, served with white rice

name: Sinigang
blurb: A sour soup, most often soured with tamarind, with pork, shrimp or fish and vegetables such as kangkong, radish and string beans.
visual: a bowl of clear sour broth soup with fish or pork, leafy greens and vegetables

name: Kare-kare
blurb: A stew of oxtail, tripe or beef in a thick peanut sauce with eggplant, string beans and bok choy, eaten with a side of salty shrimp paste (bagoong).
visual: a thick orange-brown peanut stew with oxtail and green vegetables

name: Sisig
blurb: Chopped pork, traditionally from the face and ears, seasoned with calamansi, onion and chili and served sizzling on a hot plate, often with an egg on top.
visual: chopped crispy pork with onions and chili served on a sizzling plate

name: Lechon
blurb: A whole pig roasted over charcoal until the skin is crackling and golden. The centrepiece of fiestas and celebrations, with Cebu's version especially famous.
visual: a whole roasted pig with crisp golden-brown skin

name: Lechon kawali
blurb: Pork belly boiled until tender, then deep-fried until the skin blisters and crackles, chopped and dipped in a vinegar or liver sauce.
visual: chunks of deep-fried crispy pork belly

name: Pancit palabok
blurb: Thin rice noodles under a thick orange shrimp-and-annatto sauce, topped with shrimp, hard-boiled egg, crushed chicharon and spring onion.
visual: rice noodles covered in orange sauce, topped with egg, shrimp and crushed pork rind

name: Pancit
blurb: Stir-fried noodles, such as canton or bihon, with vegetables and meat or shrimp. Served at birthdays because long noodles stand for long life.
visual: stir-fried noodles with carrots, cabbage and meat or shrimp

name: Lumpia
blurb: Spring rolls. The fried kind, like lumpiang Shanghai with ground pork, is a party staple; the fresh kind (sariwa) is wrapped around vegetables with a sweet garlic sauce.
visual: golden brown fried spring rolls

name: Halo-halo
blurb: Shaved ice mixed with milk, sweet beans, jellies, fruit and leche flan, topped with ube ice cream. "Halo-halo" means "mix-mix", so you stir it before you eat.
visual: a tall glass of shaved ice with colourful toppings and purple ice cream

name: Bibingka
blurb: A soft rice cake made with coconut milk and baked on a banana leaf, topped with salted egg, cheese and grated coconut. A Christmas-season favourite after Simbang Gabi.
visual: a round flat rice cake on a banana leaf topped with salted egg and cheese

name: Puto
blurb: Small, fluffy steamed rice cakes, usually white and slightly sweet, often topped with cheese and eaten with dinuguan.
visual: small round white steamed rice cakes

name: Tinola
blurb: A light chicken soup flavoured with ginger, with green papaya or chayote and chili or malunggay leaves.
visual: a bowl of clear chicken soup with ginger, green papaya and leaves

name: Dinuguan
blurb: A savoury pork stew cooked in pig's blood with vinegar and chili, dark as chocolate. Often eaten with puto.
visual: a dark brown stew of pork in thick blood sauce with a green chili

name: Pinakbet
blurb: A vegetable stew of squash, okra, eggplant, bitter melon and string beans, seasoned with fermented fish or shrimp paste.
visual: a stew of okra, eggplant, squash and string beans with pork or shrimp

name: Bicol Express
blurb: Pork stewed in coconut milk with shrimp paste and plenty of green and red chilies, named after the Bicol region known for its spicy, coconut-rich cooking.
visual: pork stewed in creamy coconut milk with lots of green and red chili peppers

name: Longganisa
blurb: Native pork sausages, either sweet and red (hamonado) or garlicky and sour, each province with its own style. A classic breakfast with garlic rice and egg.
where: Nationwide, famous in Vigan and Lucban
visual: small reddish-brown sausages, fried, with garlic rice and egg

name: Balut
blurb: A fertilized duck egg boiled and eaten from the shell with salt or vinegar. A famous, and for many visitors daring, street food usually sold at night.
visual: a boiled duck egg cracked open in the hand showing the developing embryo

name: Turon
blurb: Slices of saba banana and sometimes jackfruit wrapped in a spring roll wrapper and fried with caramelized brown sugar.
visual: fried banana spring rolls glazed with caramelized sugar

name: Kwek-kwek
blurb: Quail eggs, hard-boiled, dipped in orange batter and deep-fried, served with a sweet or spicy vinegar dip. Tokneneng is the same with larger duck or chicken eggs.
visual: bright orange deep-fried battered eggs on sticks

name: Fish ball
blurb: Small fried balls of fish paste sold from street carts, skewered and dipped in sweet, spicy or vinegar sauce.
visual: small round fried fish balls on skewers from a street cart

name: Isaw
blurb: Chicken or pork intestines cleaned, threaded onto sticks and grilled, dipped in a spiced vinegar sauce.
visual: grilled skewers of coiled chicken intestines

name: Ube halaya
blurb: A sweet, creamy jam of purple yam (ube) cooked with milk and butter. Also a filling for cakes, ice cream and halo-halo.
visual: smooth purple jam of yam in a dish

name: Kinilaw
blurb: Raw fish or seafood "cooked" in vinegar and citrus with onion, ginger and chili. Closer to ceviche than to sashimi; beloved in the Visayas and Mindanao.
visual: chunks of raw fish in vinegar with onion, ginger and chili

name: Chicken inasal
blurb: Bacolod-style chicken marinated in calamansi, vinegar, lemongrass and ginger, basted with annatto oil and grilled over charcoal, served with rice.
visual: a grilled chicken leg quarter with orange marinade, rice and dipping sauce on a banana leaf

name: Sapin-sapin
blurb: A layered sticky rice cake made with coconut milk and coloured with ube, jackfruit and other flavours. "Sapin" means layer.
visual: a multi-coloured layered sticky rice cake in purple, yellow and white

name: Kutsinta
blurb: Chewy, brown steamed rice cakes coloured with annatto and lye water, served with grated coconut.
visual: small round chewy brown-orange steamed rice cakes with grated coconut

name: Suman
blurb: Sticky rice cooked in coconut milk, wrapped in banana or palm leaves and steamed. Eaten with sugar, latik or ripe mango.
visual: sticky rice cakes wrapped in green banana or palm leaves

name: Ensaymada
blurb: A soft, buttery brioche-like bread coiled into a spiral and topped with butter, sugar and often grated cheese; inherited from Spain's ensaïmada.
visual: a soft coiled sweet bread topped with butter, sugar and cheese

name: Pandesal
blurb: The Filipino breakfast bread: soft, slightly sweet rolls coated in fine breadcrumbs, best eaten warm from the bakery in the morning.
visual: small golden bread rolls dusted with breadcrumbs

name: Champorado
blurb: Sweet chocolate rice porridge made with tablea (pure cocoa tablets), poured with milk and traditionally paired with salty dried fish (tuyo).
visual: a bowl of chocolate rice porridge with a swirl of milk

name: Ginataan
blurb: A sweet stew cooked in coconut milk (gata) with sticky rice balls, sago, sweet potato and jackfruit; there are savoury ginataang dishes too.
visual: a bowl of creamy white coconut milk stew with sago pearls and sweet potato

name: Lugaw
blurb: A comforting rice porridge. Arroz caldo adds chicken and ginger, goto adds tripe, and it is topped with toasted garlic, egg and spring onion.
visual: a bowl of thick rice porridge topped with toasted garlic and a boiled egg

name: Batchoy
blurb: A noodle soup from Iloilo with pork innards, chicharon, egg and a rich broth. The La Paz market version is the best known.
visual: a bowl of noodle soup topped with pork, crushed chicharon and spring onion

name: Kaldereta
blurb: A rich tomato-based stew of goat or beef with potatoes, carrots, bell peppers and liver spread, often with olives and cheese.
visual: a red-orange tomato stew of meat with potatoes, carrots, peppers and olives
